post.caption: The first princess cut was a flop. In 1961, London cutter Arpad Nagy named his square diamond the princess cut, but it did not sell, and today it is called the profile cut. Then, in the late 1970s, three Israeli cutters tried again with a square diamond that had brilliant facets, like a round one. Seen from the side it looks like an upside down pyramid, and boomerang shaped chevron facets on the bottom add sparkle. The trio first sold it as the Quadrillion. For decades it ranked second only to the round cut. Photo: Stephen Durham, CC BY 2.0
